stories.title: KPMG consulting head says AI is killing the advice business
stories.summary: KPMG global head of consulting Svilena Tzekova says AI is undermining the firm's business model, noting that clients can now access knowledge that previously required months of consulting work. She stated that the firm's traditional advice-based revenue stream is literally nonexistent anymore. Advice is now a commodity.

stories.title: How accounting firms became consulting giants
stories.summary: Accounting firms expanded into consulting to follow the money. Wartime demands introduced accountants to complex management systems, while the 1950s computer boom invited firms to design the systems they once audited. By the 1980s, audit-fee competition and corporate restructuring made advisory services the primary revenue engine.

stories.title: Big Four accounting firms shrink as mid-tier practices grow
stories.summary: Australia's top 100 accounting firms saw combined revenue rise 3 percent to $15.6 billion in 2025-26. While mid-tier practices grew 9 percent, the Big Four contracted 1.6 percent amid governance scandals and sluggish consulting demand. Partner numbers fell across the sector as the market split.

stories.title: Most AI work does not require expensive frontier models
stories.summary: A report from Wharton and Accenture suggests companies are overspending on AI. While firms often deploy the most powerful models for every task, research shows 90 percent of AI-ready work is routine. Only 11 percent of tasks actually require the bleeding edge. Efficiency is currently optional.

stories.title: Workers report AI productivity gains while profits remain elusive
stories.summary: A McKinsey survey found 80 percent of employees believe AI makes them more productive. However, only 37 percent of organizations can link the technology to positive earnings, a figure unchanged from last year. The finance department is still waiting for the invoice to pay off.

stories.title: Re:think: Don’t just ‘peanut butter’ AI on top. Redesign roles and processes. - McKinsey & Company
McKinsey says agentic AI can cut planning time by 83 percent
stories.summary: McKinsey reports that agentic AI could reduce business planning workloads by 83 percent and forecast errors by 50 percent. The firm suggests that combining predictive models with AI agents allows companies to move from periodic forecasting to continuous decision-making. The manual work is being automated away.

stories.title: McKinsey study claims agentic AI reduces planning errors
stories.summary: McKinsey reports that agentic AI can reduce business planning workloads by 83 percent and forecast errors by 50 percent. The findings, based on a life sciences company implementation, suggest that combining predictive models with AI agents helps organizations move away from periodic, manual forecasting exercises.

stories.title: McKinsey: agentic AI could change business planning, cut busywork 83% - NewsBytes
McKinsey suggests banks could recover AI investments in 10 months
stories.summary: McKinsey reports that banks deploying AI agents could recover their initial investment in about 10 months and generate 2.9 times their outlay over three years. The firm notes that success depends on scale, controls, and cost discipline. The agents are expected to handle everyday work.

stories.title: Bain survey finds 33 percent of companies see AI results
stories.summary: Bain's August 2026 survey found 33 percent of companies have achieved measurable revenue or cost results from AI, up 10 percentage points from last year. Respondents reported that AI met or exceeded expectations in 76 percent of use cases. The returns are finally appearing on the spreadsheet.

stories.title: Healthcare consumers and clinicians are increasingly dissatisfied
stories.summary: Nearly one-third of consumers sought care at a different health system in the last year for better access. Meanwhile, clinician satisfaction is at an all-time low, with one in four physicians wanting to switch employers. AI is being positioned as a potential accelerant for change.

stories.title: Physician satisfaction hits record low as patient loyalty wavers
stories.summary: Bain reports that physician satisfaction has reached its lowest point since 2017, with one in four doctors looking to leave their employer. While health systems are investing in AI, only 40 percent of administrators can clearly measure the return on that technology. The loyalty is up for grabs.

stories.title: Healthcare providers struggle to measure AI investment returns
stories.summary: Healthcare administrators are dedicating up to 25 percent of IT spend to AI, yet only 40 percent can clearly measure the return on that investment. While nearly two-thirds expect meaningful results within three years, actual gains remain uneven. The metrics are currently catching up to the spending.

stories.title: KPMG India CEO outlook highlights resilience and AI investment
stories.summary: CEOs in India remain confident about growth despite economic and geopolitical uncertainty. The KPMG 2026 outlook shows leaders are prioritizing cybersecurity and AI adoption to strengthen resilience. Investment in people and digital capabilities is being framed as a strategy to turn current volatility into future growth.

stories.title: Indian music streaming hits 6 trillion songs as creator pay lags
stories.summary: Indians streamed nearly six trillion songs in 2025, but making a full-time career in music is becoming harder. EY and IPRS report that only 55 percent of composers and lyricists now work full-time, down from 60 percent in 2023. The industry value grew 45 percent, but the creators remain.

stories.title: India music economy value grows 45 percent to 17,400 crore
stories.summary: India's music creator economy generated 17,400 crore in gross economic value in 2025, a 45 percent increase over 2023. Digital platforms accounted for 52 percent of this value, and employment in the organized segment rose 50 percent. It is a good time to be in music.

stories.title: India music economy reaches $1.8 billion
stories.summary: India's music economy generated $1.8 billion in 2025, a 45% increase over two years, according to an EY study. Digital platforms drove 52% of this value, while independent artists captured 43% of digital listening. Indians streamed nearly six trillion tracks last year. The industry is finding its rhythm.

stories.title: Luxury goods sales forecast to rise 2% in 2026
stories.summary: Personal luxury goods sales are forecast to reach €367 billion in 2026, a 2% increase, according to Bain & Company. Jewelry sales are expected to rise 8% to 10% as consumers show a clear perception of value. Headwinds from the Iran war remain a factor for the industry.

stories.title: Global luxury spending remains stable at €1.5 trillion
stories.summary: Global luxury spending remains stable at €1.5 trillion in 2026 despite geopolitical and macroeconomic uncertainty, according to Bain & Company. The firm notes that longevity is opening new opportunities as consumers live longer, healthier lives. Luxury is now being asked to tap into new universes to sustain growth.

Purpose Brand acquires MassiveMinds for AI research
stories.summary: Chicago communications consultancy Purpose Brand has acquired MassiveMinds to integrate AI-assisted research into its agency work. Founder Patrick Palmer joins the firm as president and chief strategy officer. The company says it is buying research expertise rather than another conventional PR shop. Financial terms remain undisclosed.

stories.title: Purpose Brand adds AI strategy with MassiveMinds acquisition
stories.summary: Purpose Brand has acquired MassiveMinds, a research consultancy founded by Patrick Palmer. The deal integrates AI-enabled research processes into the agency's existing marketing and public relations workflows. Palmer joins as president and chief strategy officer, bringing 35 years of experience to the Chicago-based firm.

stories.title: Purpose Brand integrates AI research via MassiveMinds deal
stories.summary: Purpose Brand has acquired MassiveMinds to incorporate custom AI approaches into its marketing and communications workflows. Founder Patrick Palmer joins the consultancy as president and chief strategy officer. The firm says the move powers human creativity with data-backed precision. Financial details of the acquisition were not disclosed.

stories.title: Steer acquires maritime consultancy Mercator
stories.summary: UK-based infrastructure consultancy Steer has acquired Kirkland-based Mercator. The deal adds specialist maritime and freight advisory services to Steer's North American practice. Mercator has completed more than 150 commercial due diligence projects since 2000. The firm will continue to operate under its existing brand name.

stories.title: Steer expands infrastructure practice with Mercator purchase
stories.summary: Global infrastructure consultancy Steer has acquired US-based Mercator International. The firm adds specialist expertise in ports, maritime, and freight advisory to its North American business. Mercator will retain its brand and leadership team. The consultancy has completed hundreds of assignments globally, including work on port masterplans and traffic forecasts.

stories.title: Finyx Group acquires Entec Si
stories.summary: Technology and transformation consultancy Finyx Group has acquired Birmingham-based Entec Si. The deal expands Finyx's presence in local government and the not-for-profit sector. Entec Si, founded in 1996, brings a core team of approximately 20 professionals to the group. The firm focuses on digital and organisational change programmes.

stories.title: DJH acquires two Sutton Coldfield accountancy firms
stories.summary: DJH has acquired Hill Talbot and Haslehursts, adding more than 30 experts to its group. The move provides the firm with its first base in Sutton Coldfield. DJH now employs nearly 1,000 people across 26 offices, recently entering the top 30 UK accountancy firms for the first time.

stories.title: 3LS acquires Accreditation Guru
stories.summary: Professional services firm 3LS has acquired New York-based consultancy Accreditation Guru. The company paid an undisclosed sum for the business. The acquisition follows a trend of consolidation within the professional services sector. The firm has not commented on the specific strategic goals behind the purchase.

stories.title: Decasult acquires risk management firm BF Strategy
stories.summary: Montreal-based construction consultancy Decasult has acquired project risk management firm BF Strategy. The boutique consultancy, founded in 2015, provides decision support and governance for complex infrastructure projects. Decasult described the acquisition of the 20-employee firm as a significant milestone in its growth trajectory.

stories.title: eClerx to acquire RegEdge for $12 million
stories.summary: Mumbai-based eClerx is acquiring US regulatory consultancy RegEdge for up to $12 million in cash. RegEdge, which reported $5.1 million in 2025 revenue, assists financial institutions with compliance and risk management. The deal is expected to close within two weeks and adds regulatory depth to the eClerx portfolio.

stories.title: Knowmad Mood acquires Danwor
stories.summary: Knowmad Mood has acquired 100% of the Argentine consulting firm Danwor for €5.45 million.

stories.title: RSB Group plans 4,000 crore rupee IPO
stories.summary: Bain-backed RSB Group is reportedly planning an IPO of approximately 4,000 crore rupees, with a draft prospectus expected in December. The company has appointed three banks to manage the issue. Five new investors recently acquired a minority stake in the firm ahead of the proposed public offering.

stories.title: India manufacturing sector marks 80th independence anniversary
stories.summary: India's manufacturing sector is being positioned as a global hub following 12 years of reforms under the Make in India vision. The government has introduced initiatives including the Production Linked Incentive scheme and the National Logistics Policy to support growth in sectors ranging from pharmaceuticals to heavy machinery.

stories.title: Battery PLI scheme reaches 1.4 GWh capacity
stories.summary: India's Production Linked Incentive scheme for Advanced Chemistry Cell batteries has developed 1.4 gigawatt-hours of manufacturing capacity against a 50 gigawatt-hour target. Commercial production has yet to begin. The assessment cites technological limitations and import dependence as reasons for the slow progress. The target remains distant.

stories.title: India’s PLI scheme adds 24GW of solar module manufacturing capacity: NITI Aayog - PV Tech
NITI Aayog reports on PLI scheme progress
stories.summary: NITI Aayog reports that India's 14 Production Linked Incentive schemes have reached 76 percent of their investment target and 64 percent of their production target. The assessment covers a period representing 58 percent of the aggregate scheme tenure. Employment figures are currently lagging behind the broader investment momentum.

stories.title: Biogas sector advised to focus on efficiency
stories.summary: A report by EY-Parthenon and the Confederation of Indian Industry suggests that India's compressed biogas sector should focus on operational efficiency rather than government price support. Higher plant utilization and reduced transportation costs are identified as the primary drivers for long-term profitability in the sector.

stories.summary: Accenture LearnVantage and Google Cloud are partnering to bring AI training to over 1,000 schools and colleges in India. The initiative includes AI labs and certifications in generative and agentic AI. The companies have not yet disclosed the names of participating institutions or a rollout schedule.

stories.title: Accenture India freezes salary hikes while offering bonuses
stories.summary: Accenture has introduced performance-linked bonuses of up to 26 percent for top-performing employees in India as part of its November 2026 rewards cycle. Regular salary increments and promotions remain largely on hold. The company is prioritizing variable payouts over broader increases in fixed salary costs.

stories.title: Boutique firms challenge major consultancies for B-school talent
stories.summary: Boutique consulting firms are increasingly competing with global strategy consultancies and the Big Four for talent at India's leading business schools. Over 40 percent of students at these institutions now prefer consulting roles. The appeal is attributed to high compensation and the brand value of the firms.

stories.title: IIMs report full summer placement coverage
stories.summary: Indian Institutes of Management report 100 percent placement for their 2026-2028 cohorts, with monthly stipends reaching 3.5 lakh rupees. The schools describe these roles as strategic pipelines for pre-placement offers, allowing students to secure full-time positions before graduation. The economy remains in upheaval, but the pipelines are open.
